rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 – Statewide cap on annual rent increases (blocked from Nov. 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: The proposed initiative would have capped annual rent increases on covered dwelling units at the lesser of the annual CPI increase or 5%, and repealed the statutory ban on rent control. The SJC ruled in Cella v. Attorney General that it may not appear on the November 2026 ballot because of its religious-facility exemption.
rules.coverage_text: All dwelling units leased for residential (not commercial) use, subject to five exemptions.

exemption_tests.description: Dwelling units in owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units.
Dwelling units whose rents are regulated by a public authority (a mobile housing voucher does not count as regulation).
Dwelling units rented primarily to transient guests for less than 14 consecutive days.
Dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes.
Dwelling units whose first residential certificate of occupancy is less than 10 years old, for 10 years from issuance of the certificate.

rules.exemptions_text: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, publicly regulated units, short-term/transient rentals, facilities operated solely for educational, religious or nonprofit purposes, and units with a certificate of occupancy less than 10 years old.
rules.key_value: Lesser of annual CPI increase or 5%
rules.citation: Initiative Petition 25-21; Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
rules.ambiguity_note: Blog notes proponents may re-file after removing the religious exemption; as of the ruling the petition cannot appear on the Nov. 2026 ballot.

rules.title: Statutory ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P)
rules.requirement: Massachusetts statute broadly prohibits any regulatory scheme based upon or implementing rent control, defined to include any regulation requiring below-market rents for residential properties. This ban remains in place because the repeal initiative was blocked.
rules.coverage_text: Statewide prohibition on rent control regulation of residential properties.
rules.quoted_span: General Laws c. 40P, § 2, "broadly prohibits any regulatory scheme based upon or implementing rent control."
rules.ambiguity_note: Described by a secondary source discussing a court opinion; enactment date not stated in this chunk.
